explanation: Early ramen shops in Tokyo and Yokohama's Chinatown were run by Chinese cooks, and the dish was long called chuka soba, Chinese soba.

claims.text: Ramen developed in Japan from Chinese wheat-noodle soups introduced by Chinese cooks.
Ramen did not develop from noodle soups brought by Korean, Thai or Vietnamese cooks.
Early ramen shops in Tokyo and Yokohama were run by Chinese cooks.
Ramen was long called chuka soba, which means Chinese soba.
